title: Hamble-le-Rice Whitley Memorial
location_name: Priory Church of St Andrew the Apostle, Hamble-le-Rice, Hampshire
memorial_details: Plaque to an eminent British aircraft engineer and his two sons, both killed in WWII, in the Priory Church of St Andrew the Apostle, Hamble-le-Rice, Hampshire.
narrative: Whitley Z6576 of 102 Squadron, coded DY-?, departed Topcliffe at 2224 on 26 July 1941 for Hannover. The aircraft was intercepted at 2200m over the North Sea, 10km west of De Kooy, by Oberleutnant Egmont Prinz zur Lippe-Weissenfeld of IV/NJG1, his 11th claim. The memorial in Hamble-le-Rice commemorates an eminent British aircraft engineer (possibly Sir Edwin Alliott Verdon-Roe, founder of Avro — verify) and his two sons, both killed in WWII, one of whom was aboard Z6576.
cause_of_loss: Shot down by night fighter — Oblt Egmont Prinz zur Lippe-Weissenfeld (IV/NJG1), his 11th claim
community_connection: The memorial commemorates a prominent aircraft engineer and his two sons, both of whom died serving in WWII.
notes: Post suggests the engineer may be Sir Edwin Alliott Verdon-Roe — verify. Post records Z6576 as a Whitley but notes '102 Sqn flew Whitleys' while calling it a Manchester in the text — Whitley is correct for 102 Sqn in 1941. CWGC and Chorley give the loss date as 26/07/41.
